[[File:Willmore conjecture - perfect doughnut.png|thumb|The torus with minimal Willmore energy, with major radius {{math|{{radic|2}}}} and minor radius 1<ref name="proof"/>]]
In [[differential geometry]], the '''Willmore conjecture''' is a [[lower bound]] on the [[Willmore energy]] of a [[torus]]. It is named after the [[England|English]] [[mathematician]] [[Tom Willmore]], who [[conjecture]]d it in 1965.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Willmore|first=Thomas J.|title=Note on embedded surfaces|journal=Analele Ştiinţifice ale Universităţii "Al. I. Cuza" din Iaşi, Secţiunea I a Matematică|year=1965|volume=11B|pages=493–496|mr=0202066}}</ref> A proof by [[Fernando Codá Marques]] and [[André Neves]] was announced in 2012 and published in 2014.<ref name="proof"/><ref name="morgan"/>

==Background==
{{main|Willmore energy}}
Let ''v''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''M''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>3</sup> be a [[smooth function|smooth]] [[immersion (mathematics)|immersion]] of a [[compact space|compact]], [[orientability|orientable surface]].  Giving ''M'' the [[Riemannian metric]] induced by ''v'', let ''H''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''M''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R''' be the [[mean curvature]] (the [[arithmetic mean]] of the [[principal curvature]]s ''κ''<sub>1</sub> and ''κ''<sub>2</sub> at each point) and let ''K'' be the [[Gaussian curvature]].  In this notation, the ''Willmore energy'' ''W''(''M'') of ''M'' is given by

:<math> W(M) = \int_M H^2 \, dA - \int_M K \, dA. </math>

It is not hard to prove that the Willmore energy satisfies ''W''(''M'')&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0, with equality [[if and only if]] ''M'' is an embedded round [[sphere]].

==Statement==

Calculation of ''W''(''M'') for a few examples suggests that there should be a better bound than ''W''(''M'')&nbsp;≥&nbsp;4''π'' for surfaces with [[genus (topology)|genus]] ''g''(''M'')&nbsp;>&nbsp;0.  In particular, calculation of ''W''(''M'') for tori with various symmetries led Willmore to propose in 1965 the following conjecture, which now bears his name

: For every smooth immersed torus ''M'' in '''R'''<sup>3</sup>, ''W''(''M'')&nbsp;≥&nbsp;2''π''<sup>2</sup>.

In 1982, [[Peter Wai-Kwong Li]] and [[Shing-Tung Yau]] proved the conjecture in the non-embedded case, showing that if <math>f:\Sigma\to S^3</math> is an immersion of a compact surface, which is ''not'' an embedding, then ''W''(''M'') is at least 8''π''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Peter |last2=Yau |first2=Shing Tung |title=A new conformal invariant and its applications to the Willmore conjecture and the first eigenvalue of compact surfaces |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |date=1982 |volume=69 |issue=2 |pages=269–291|mr=0674407|doi=10.1007/BF01399507|bibcode=1982InMat..69..269L }}</ref>

In 2012, [[Fernando Codá Marques]] and [[André Neves]] proved the conjecture in the embedded case, using the [[Almgren–Pitts min-max theory|Almgren–Pitts min-max theory of minimal surfaces]].<ref name="morgan">[[Frank Morgan (mathematician)|Frank Morgan]] (2012) "[http://www.huffingtonpost.com/frank-morgan/math-finds-the-best-dough_b_1331844.html Math Finds the Best Doughnut]", ''[[The Huffington Post]]''</ref><ref name="proof">{{cite journal |last1=Marques |first1=Fernando C. |first2=André |last2=Neves |title=Min-max theory and the Willmore conjecture |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |year=2014 |arxiv=1202.6036 | doi = 10.4007/annals.2014.179.2.6 |volume=179 |issue=2 |pages=683–782|mr=3152944}}</ref> Prior to the proof of Marques and Neves, the Willmore conjecture had already been proved for many special cases, such as [[Tube torus|tube tori]] (by Willmore himself), and for [[Torus|tori]] of [[Surface of revolution|revolution]] (by Langer & Singer).<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Langer|first1=Joel|last2=Singer|first2=David|doi=10.1112/blms/16.5.531|issue=5|journal=The Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|mr=751827|pages=531–534|title=Curves in the hyperbolic plane and mean curvature of tori in 3-space|volume=16|year=1984}}</ref>
